# Inlet

> Inlet is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS app that keeps the Downloads folder clean and finds files you describe in plain words. It runs entirely on the Mac: no account, no cloud, no analytics, no network access.

- Tidy: sorts files into category folders (Images, Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations, Videos, Audio, Archives, Installers, Code, Design, Fonts, Keys & Certs), automatically once a download finishes (Auto mode) or after a preview (Manual mode, the default). Never touches in-progress downloads.
- Find: press ⌘F and describe a file, e.g. "pdfs from github last week" or "big videos I haven't opened in a month". Uses macOS Spotlight and Inlet's own records, not an AI service.
- Remembers the website and app each download came from, even after unzipping.
- Rules by name, extension, size, age, source website, Finder kind or text inside the file; rules can rename files.
- Safety: never deletes or overwrites; every move can be undone (⌘Z, menu bar, Activity page); removed files are held 30 days.
- Requirements: macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel. One universal .pkg installer. Not signed with a paid Apple certificate, so macOS asks for confirmation once on first open.
